title: SCAN v0.29: deterministic coverage and gaps projection
body:
## Production-readiness Stage 1: coverage / gaps

This PR forks released SCAN v0.28.0 into the v0.29 candidate and implements only the first production-readiness tranche.

### Added

- automatic `coverage_report.json`
- compact `coverage_report.md`
- unresolved `gaps.md`
- explicit `scan-body coverage-report` regeneration command
- projection-manifest sealing for all three outputs
- refresh support after legitimate canonical overlay/reconstruction promotion
- v0.29 release qualification now requires these outputs
- tracked production-readiness gate document

### Authority boundary

`scan_index.sqlite` remains canonical.

The new projection:
- opens canonical data read-only;
- cannot promote or downgrade MAPPED/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN;
- reuses existing surface/effect closure rather than reimplementing it;
- retains canonical IDs/evidence IDs;
- deliberately emits **no scalar confidence score**.

### Executed evidence so far

Dedicated v0.29 candidate workflow:
- **163 passed, 1 skipped**
- duplicate coverage-report bytes: PASS
- projection manifest verification: PASS
- canonical SQLite row determinism: PASS
- v0.28 → v0.29 canonical row parity on the qualification fixture: PASS
- exact report-count reconciliation to SQLite: PASS

Frozen NotepadNext/Moji v0.28→v0.29 calibration is running as the remaining Stage-1 real-specimen gate.

### Explicitly out of scope

No uncertainty challenger, triage ranking, layered-provenance redesign, parity-scenario system, runtime validation, or other later roadmap stage is included in this PR.

The inherited v0.28 `PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json` was removed; v0.29 is not release-sealed.

title: Certify native resident lifecycle on disposable runners
body:
## Objective

Advance issue #16 from fixture-only registration checks to actual native OS lifecycle evidence in disposable GitHub-hosted environments. No service is installed on the creator's PC and no real organism SELF is changed.

## Implementation

- Add separate read-only-permission Windows/Linux Python 3.12 workflow with a ten-minute job bound and no provider secrets.
- Opt-in test refuses normal local/self-hosted execution and keeps generated NESTs under RUNNER_TEMP.
- Use production registration/removal, real local organ runtime and newly born disposable encrypted Body; require startup, communication, restart, already-stopped removal, preserved Primer/native bytes and VCW validity.
- Linux tests automatic systemd on-failure restart following SIGKILL and zero-status cooperative stop. Windows tests explicit Task Scheduler forced stop/start, not graceful stop or automatic recovery.
- Retain JUnit results only; preserve ownership checks during cleanup. Disposable hosted machines are discarded on failure.
- Update PLAN.md, lifecycle evidence and changelog without changing production-completion claims.
- Real Windows testing exposed omitted default RunLevel XML; accept absence but reject explicit elevated, empty or unknown values. Keep owner/action checks intact and mirror the correction into the Hermes seed.
- Windows installation now immediately starts the verified task, matching Linux. The native test no longer supplies an initial task start. Verification/start failure retains pending intent and refuses unsafe execution or rollback.

## Verification scope

Local code-quality and process regression checks run with native registration deliberately skipped. The new native workflow and existing full Windows/Linux matrix, security and pinned-Hermes gates must pass before merge. This PR does not close issue #16: login/reboot certification, Windows automatic restart, partial-removal recovery, storage fencing and crash-atomic admission remain open.

Local final regression: 194 passed, 3 platform/opt-in skips; Ruff, public audit and seed checksums passed. Both native jobs passed at commit 30647be; final head tightens immediate-start verification and must pass again. Both native checks have been added to protected-main requirements without removing any existing checks or app bindings.

title: Guard resident registration ownership and failure evidence
body:
## Outcome

Advance issue #16 with registration ownership and failure safeguards. This is not full resident lifecycle certification and does not install a service or birth a real organism on the creator's PC.

## Changes and reasons

- Refuse local/unit collisions and remove Windows task creation's forced-replacement option. A NEST must not overwrite an unrelated OS registration.
- Preserve a pending receipt before OS changes, then mark registered only after verification. Retain failure evidence rather than guessing whether rollback is safe.
- Rederive removal targets from the NEST and validate strict bounded receipts, expected runner bytes, current task SID/action/privilege or exact loaded unit with no drop-ins.
- Check Linux loaded configuration before service start. Request Windows task stop before deletion; stop failure prevents deletion.
- Keep legacy receipts readable and missing runners visible; distinguish receipt-only status from actual running-state proof.
- Synchronize PLAN.md, coding contract, resident evidence documentation, changelog, Hermes runtime payload and seed checksums.

## Verification

- Local Windows suite: 188 passed, 2 explicit platform skips (real POSIX SIGTERM and unavailable symlink privilege).
- Ruff and whitespace checks passed.
- All seed checksums, manifest payload hashes and normalized source/runtime mirror verified.
- New OS-fixture tests cover altered receipts, XML/owner/action drift, collisions, unsupported paths, overridden units, pending evidence, stop failure and bounded noninteractive command execution.
- Required CI must pass before merge, including Windows/Linux Python 3.11–3.13, CodeQL and pinned Hermes gates.

## Remaining boundaries

Native task XML variants, already-stopped task behavior, actual service-manager restart/removal and interrupted-removal recovery still require disposable native certification. Preflight checks are not a transaction with the OS, a concurrent-attacker guarantee, stale-writer fencing or an atomic Heartbeat checkpoint. No automatic recovery/deletion of uncertain installations is added. Issue #16 remains open.

title: Add cooperative resident shutdown and preserve scheduled maintenance
body:
## Summary

Advance issue #16 with cooperative CLI shutdown and reliable maintenance scheduling.

- Signal handlers set a flag only, without locks or I/O; restore previous handlers
  on return/failure and refuse non-main-thread installation.
- Recheck stop after bounded idle slices and before new full Heartbeats. Complete
  started work; do not convert a failed beat into successful shutdown.
- Preserve the configured observation cadence; consider scheduled work even when
  file observation fails. Coalesce due/message collision and avoid response echoes.
- Keep runtime, PLAN, technical contract, resident evidence and Hermes seed aligned.

## Evidence

- Local Ruff passed; 144 tests passed and one real POSIX signal test was correctly
  skipped on Windows.
- New deterministic cadence/stop tests and actual Linux SIGTERM test run through
  the existing six-platform CI matrix.
- Existing forced-stop/restart, encrypted VCW, Primer and native Body proofs remain.
- All seed manifests/checksums and runtime copies are synchronized.

## Limits

Not full resident certification: actual native service registration/removal,
storage writer fencing, atomic publication, async cancellation and hard overall
shutdown deadlines remain open. Windows forced termination is not graceful
SIGTERM delivery. No live credentials, real organism birth or creator-machine
resident registration is involved. See `docs/RESIDENT_HEART.md` for exact scope.

title: Run resident Heart from NEST-local organs
body:
The generated resident Heart launcher previously imported the constructor's globally installed `mantleos` package. After assimilation, this could execute a different runtime from the organs shipped inside the NEST.

Launch Python in isolated mode and explicitly load `mantle/runtime/mantleos`. Refuse installation or startup when the local package is missing or its directory is redirected. Include the runtime and interpreter in the registration receipt and refresh the public Hermes seed.

Validation: 73 local tests, Ruff, public-tree audit, and seed checksum verification pass. A real disposable subprocess with authenticated encryption exercises startup, committed communication without MIND, forced stop/restart, recovery of a pending host receipt, unchanged sealed Primer, and native Body output. Additional tests cover unrelated working directories, Python import-path interference, missing organs, and Windows/Linux registration command construction.

Advances #16. Task Scheduler/systemd installation and automatic restart are still unverified; registration tests remain mocked. No OS resident registration is performed by this test suite.
